label: O(n)
why: while guard calls SumDiv1306(counts,day) inline each iteration (short-circuited with day<=maxC+1); charging it needs the guard rewritten into a precomputed ghost-tracked boolean, and the true cost maxC*|counts| is not linear in any single input (worst case ~k^2 when counts split as one big group + many singletons) -- no O(n) scaffold reachable in budget

why: CeilSqrt does a value-bounded binary search (doubling to find hi, then bisecting): tying the per-iteration Pow2/Log2 growth invariants together into one closed log(x) step bound across both phases did not close within budget

why: linear-search loop `while s*s<target` is genuinely value-bounded (O(sqrt(n)), not O(1), per the value-counts-as-parameter convention); the label is likely unreachable and even a loose linear bound needs two case-split implication invariants over nonlinear s*s that Z3 would not close in budget

label: O(n)
why: Solve computes d, b, y through a chain (d=FloorDiv(s-1,2), b=triangular(d)+1, y=k-b) where RepStr is then called on x-y-1 and y; bounding those arguments back in terms of the row (nn, k) needs 4-5 chained nonlinear inequality lemmas (sqrt bound, FloorDiv bound, triangular-number bound, subtraction bound) to avoid the bound blowing up sign-wise, which does not fit in the per-row budget.

label: O(n)
why: the fixed-length prime loop (bounded by |primes|=54, independent of n) accumulates `last` as a product of up to 53 literal primes before the final l1[n-1]:=last write; bounding |IntToString(last)| for the Join/SumLen charge needs a hoisted top-level Primes() constant plus a partial-product monotonicity lemma over literal seq indices -- more scaffolding than the budget allows
